headline: Hormuz Diplomacy Lifts Pre-Market Mood as Retailers Nurse Deep Tuesday Wounds
body_html:
Futures point modestly higher Wednesday morning after oil prices retreated roughly two dollars overnight on reports that Iran and Oman are in active talks to establish a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz. The prospective opening eases one of the market's most persistent macro overhangs — six months of energy trench warfare that has battered European gas inventories and broadly lifted U.S. liquefied-natural-gas export volumes. Traders will be watching crude benchmarks closely at the open; any further de-escalation language from either party could reinforce the relief trade across energy-sensitive sectors.

Tuesday's session closed on a split note. Semiconductors led all sectors with a gain of 1.67%, while homebuilders added 0.93% and healthcare rose 0.56%. The other side of the ledger was rougher: software dropped 1.0%, energy fell 0.78%, and industrials slid 0.54%. Breadth was negative — 285 names declined against 262 advancers in our 549-name universe — underscoring that Tuesday's modest sector wins masked meaningful underlying churn.

The session's defining moment was Dick's Sporting Goods, which collapsed 30.68%, dragging peer Academy Sports + Outdoors down 5.80% in sympathy. Burlington Stores shed 4.65%, rounding out a punishing day for consumer and retail names. With the IMF's managing director flagging fiscal fragility even as the global economy absorbs the energy shock, investors head into Wednesday's open with geopolitical diplomacy as the primary catalyst to monitor.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Corridor Talks Knock $2 Off Crude Overnight
briefs.body: Iran and Oman are discussing a temporary maritime passage through the Strait of Hormuz, sources familiar with the negotiations say. The prospect of even a limited reopening sent oil prices down roughly two dollars in overnight trading. Traffic through the strait has been running below its ten-day average, keeping energy markets on edge.

briefs.headline: Dick's Sporting Goods Suffers a Historic Single-Session Collapse
briefs.body: Shares of Dick's Sporting Goods plummeted 30.68% on Tuesday in one of the steepest single-day drops in the retailer's history. The selloff pulled Academy Sports + Outdoors down 5.80% and contributed to broader weakness in consumer names, including a 4.65% decline at off-price chain Burlington Stores.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Names Outrun the Tape as Chips Stay in Favor
briefs.body: The semiconductor sector rose 1.67% on Tuesday, the best performance of any group in our coverage universe. Analog specialist Semtech gained 5.47% and MaxLinear added 5.70%, suggesting the cohort retains buying interest even as broader breadth tilted negative.

briefs.headline: Bond-Market Sentiment Shifts as Options Traders Position for a Rally
briefs.body: A notable build in bullish options positioning suggests a growing contingent of investors believes the prolonged bond sell-off may be approaching an inflection point. Large wagers on a rate-market rebound dominated options activity, drawing attention ahead of any fresh fiscal or inflation data that could validate or undercut the thesis.

briefs.headline: Trump Sends Saudi Nuclear Cooperation Proposal to Congress
briefs.body: The White House has formally transmitted a Saudi Arabian civil-nuclear cooperation framework to Capitol Hill, conditioning U.S. support on Riyadh extending diplomatic recognition to Israel. The move adds a new layer of complexity to Middle East diplomacy already strained by the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict and Hormuz negotiations.

briefs.headline: Two Software Names Face Critical Tests of Their Recent Rebounds
briefs.body: A pair of software stocks in our coverage universe enter Wednesday at pivotal technical and fundamental junctures, with the durability of their recent rallies now under scrutiny. The broader software sector finished Tuesday as the worst-performing group, off 1.0%, providing a challenging backdrop for names still attempting to establish recovery momentum.
